I’ve been farming these 4.1 mu for 8 years. I split the land into 2 mu for wheat-maize double cropping and 2.1 mu for cotton. Last year my wheat did about 460 jin per mu, maize did around 580 jin per mu, and cotton gave me about 280 jin per mu of seed cotton. This year I’m not changing much — if it worked, why gamble?

For wheat, I plant an improved variety, whatever the seed dealer says is selling well from last year. Before sowing I spread about 50 kg per mu of compound fertilizer as base, then I top-dress twice with urea — once when the wheat greens up and again at jointing stage. That comes to about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu, 7 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium total. I irrigate four times from the well: green-up water, jointing water, heading water, and one light irrigation at grain filling. The electricity bill hurts, but dry wheat is a disaster. Two pesticide sprays — one herbicide early, one for insects if I see them. I do rotary tillage before I sow wheat in October, break the soil fine.

For maize, I only plant hybrid seed. Everyone around here uses hybrid, and I learned that lesson fast. I plant right after wheat harvest in early June, almost no tillage — just strip into the wheat stubble so I don’t miss the planting window. I put down 20 kg nitrogen per mu, 5 kg phosphorus, 6 kg potassium. My neighbor used 18 kg nitrogen last year and his maize was a bit yellow and short. Saving 10 yuan on fertilizer and losing 50 kg of yield is stupid. I irrigate three times: at sowing, at big trumpet stage, and at grain filling. Two pesticide applications. If the weather is normal I expect 600 kg per mu.

For cotton, it takes the most watching. I plough the 2.1 mu cotton field in spring to warm the soil and break the hardpan. I use an improved variety — not the old traditional types anymore, the improved ones have better boll weight. I apply 15 kg nitrogen per mu, 6 kg phosphorus, 8 kg potassium. Cotton needs more potassium or the bolls drop before opening. I irrigate four times and spray pesticide five times — aphids, bollworm, spider mites, you name it. Cotton is picky. I expect about 300 kg per mu of seed cotton.

With seven people at home and some working outside, I have family labor but cash is tight. Every bag of fertilizer is real money. But I’d rather put down one extra bag than risk a bad harvest — a bad harvest means I lose the whole year, not just a few dozen yuan.
